per_option_rationale.rationale: Student evaluates log_3(1/3) as +1 instead of -1, dropping the negative in the exponent, giving 4 + 1 = 5.
Student evaluates only log_3(81) = 4 and ignores the second term, reading the sum as log_3(81) alone.
Student evaluates only log_3(1/3) = -1 and ignores log_3(81), returning just -1 for the expression.

explanation_sections.punchline: Express each argument as a power of 3: log_3(3^4) + log_3(3^(-1)) = 4 + (-1) = 3.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply log_b(b^n) = n to each term separately. First: 81 = 3^4, so log_3(81) = 4. Second: 1/3 = 3^(-1), so log_3(1/3) = -1. Add the results.
explanation_sections.lesson: log_b(1/b) = -1 always, because 1/b = b^(-1). Never drop the negative sign.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-75 seconds. The key trap is option 2 (answer=5) from treating log_3(1/3) as +1 instead of -1.
